description.value: This study examined the neural systems underlying cognitive reappraisal of personally craved and not craved energy-dense foods, and relationships between neural activation and body mass index.

spans.text: This study examined how self-regulation of craving for tempting foods influenced self-reported desire and neural activation.

description.value: Fifty participants completed an event-related fMRI food regulation task involving a 2 × 2 Stimulus by Instruction design, followed by individual difference measures.

spans.text: The final event-related design included five trial types (Look Neutral [LN], Look Craved [LC], Look Not Craved [LNC], Regulate Craved [RC], and Regulate Not Craved [RNC]), with 20 trials for each condition totaling 100 trials, distributed across three approximately even runs with brief breaks in between.

spans.text: As shown in Figure 2A , the main effect of Regulate versus Look across both picture types (Craved, Not Craved) produced a large cluster of activation encompassing the left IFG, anterior insula, and DLPFC, which connected with another cluster in the dACC and pre-SMA. design_type.value: Event-related 2 × 2 Stimulus (Craved vs Not Craved) × Instruction (Look vs Regulate) design with a neutral condition

instructions.value: Look: focus on the pictured food, imagine it was in front of you, and think about consuming it. Regulate: focus on the food and think about it in a way that reduced desire to eat it. Participants selected one of four reappraisal strategies and used it on every Regulate trial.

stimuli.value: Pictures of low-energy-density neutral foods and energy-dense foods selected by participants as most craved or least craved.

value: Self-reported desirability rating on a 1-to-5 Likert scale
